subject: URGENT: EU 502/503 + timeouts impacting Clearline checkout
messages:
From: Claire Huang <c.huang@clearline.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ops-support@clearline.com
Date: 2028-10-14T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: URGENT: 502/503 spike + user timeouts in EU (Clearline checkout)

Jonas and team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 502/503 responses and frontend timeouts for EU traffic at ~08:45 UTC this morning. Checkout failures have jumped to ~18% of attempts for our EU customers and we’re receiving a lot of client retries which is making the symptoms worse.

What we have so far:
- First spike seen at 08:45 UTC, sustained through subsequent health-check cycles
- 502/503 errors clustered on requests proxied through eu-edge-usw-2 (trace examples attached)
- We’ve attached a short log snippet and a screenshot from our monitoring dashboard.

Attachments:
- 20281014_eu_502s_screenshot.png (image/png)
- clearline_logs_snip.txt (text/plain)

This is blocking checkout for EU customers; we need an ETA on mitigation and whether you can route traffic away from the problematic nodes. Please escalate — our ops team is standing by.

Thanks,
Claire Huang
VP Engineering, Clearline Finance
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <c.huang@clearline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-14T15:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: 502/503 spike + user timeouts in EU (Clearline checkout)

Claire — thanks for the report and the attachments. I’m very sorry you’re hitting this. I’ve looped in our SRE and regional ops leads.

Can you share one or two example trace-ids from failed requests (the x-request-id or Redwood-Trace header) so we can correlate on our side? Also, if you can temporarily suppress aggressive client-side retries that would help us stabilize traffic while we mitigate.

Immediate next steps on our side: I’m asking SRE to look at edge health + LB metrics and to consider temporary reroute or rate-limiting at the edge. I’ll update you within 30 minutes with actions.

—Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-14T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: URGENT: 502/503 spike + user timeouts in EU (Clearline checkout)

Team — forwarding Clearline’s report. TL;DR: sudden 502/503 spike impacting checkout (EU). Attachments include a monitoring screenshot and a small log snippet. Customer reports retry amplification on their side as well.

Why high priority: paying checkout flow is regressing for a large customer in EU during business hours. They want ETA and mitigation — they’ve CC’d their ops support.

Ask: please triage immediately and reply with temporary mitigation steps we can communicate (route, rate-limit, circuit-break, node drain). If you need nominal capacity increases or LB config changes, call out the ETA.

Quick references: runbook link — https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xRunbookEU_ratelimit and we have an open Ops ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-9123 (creating a dedicated incident now).

Attachments forwarded: eu_har_export.har

Thanks,
Jonas
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-14T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: URGENT: 502/503 spike + user timeouts in EU (Clearline checkout)

On 10/14/2028 15:28, Jonas Weber wrote:
> Team — forwarding Clearline’s report. TL;DR: sudden 502/503 spike impacting checkout (EU).

We’re on it — initial findings below.

Observations (first-pass):
- Edge LB (eu-edge-usw-2) shows CPU and connection queue growth starting ~08:42 UTC. Upstream pool shows increased 502s (5xx from origin) coincident with a burst of client retries.
- No config deploys in the region in the past hour. We’re seeing a confluence of heavier-than-normal small payload traffic from one Clearline origin and amplified retries.

Immediate mitigations applied (15:40 UTC):
1) Applied soft rate-limit at edge for client IPs using runbook thresholds (reduces retry amplification).
2) Began draining a small subset of unhealthy nodes and routing to warmed healthy pool in eu-edge-usw-1.
3) Triggered temporary circuit-break on the problematic origin to give downstream time to recover.

Planned next steps (ETA):
- 15:55 UTC: full traffic reroute to eu-edge-usw-1 (in progress).
- 16:10 UTC: confirm reduction in 5xx and client timeouts; monitor for recurrence.
- 17:00 UTC: if still elevated, we’ll coordinate short capacity burst provisioning (30–60min) and follow up with customer on root-cause.

I’ve attached a HAR export and linked the incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-9123.

Attachments:
- eu_har_export.har (application/http-archive)

Grace O'Connor
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <c.huang@clearline.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-14T18:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: 502/503 spike + user timeouts in EU (Clearline checkout)

Hi Claire — following up with a status update and our apology for the disruption.

What we’ve done:
- Applied edge rate-limits and routed EU traffic off the affected node pool.
- Initial metrics show 5xx rate down from ~18% to ~2.5% on checkout paths (steady improvement).
- Incident ticket: OPS-9123 for full RCA and timeline.

What we recommend on your side:
- If possible, temporarily reduce aggressive client retry behavior for the next hour to avoid amplification while we complete the RCA.

Customer-facing remediation: as a gesture for the impact during your peak, we’ll propose a one-week service credit against October invoices; I’ll share formal paperwork after we close the RCA. If you’d prefer an alternate remedy, tell me and we’ll accommodate.

We’ll keep you posted and share the RCA timeline by EOD tomorrow. Please reach out directly if you see any regression.

Thanks for your patience — Marissa will follow up on credit/contract items.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
